title: NEO-DNND: Communication-Optimized Distributed Nearest Neighbor Graph Construction
problem: Graph-based approximate nearest neighbor algorithms are memory- and time-consuming at scale. Constructing neighborhood graphs from billion-scale datasets presents significant computational and communication challenges in distributed systems.
motivation: Efficient graph-based nearest neighbor construction enables large-scale similarity search and analytics applications across distributed computing platforms.
method: NEO-DNND is a distributed NN-Descent algorithm built on MPI that optimizes network bandwidth efficiency through three key mechanisms: reducing duplicate elements in neighbor-checking iterations, increasing intra-node data sharing to leverage local DRAM, and replicating frequently-sent data to minimize communication overhead. The algorithm scales across multiple nodes while maintaining efficient resource utilization for billion-scale graph construction.
key_novelty: Communication-optimized distributed NN-Descent combining duplicate reduction and intra-node data replication to minimize network communication in graph construction.
contributions: Scalable distributed NN-Descent implementation capable of billion-scale nearest neighbor graph construction
Communication optimization mechanisms reducing duplicate elements and maximizing intra-node data reuse
41.7X performance improvement at 32 nodes over single-node execution and 6.0X speedup over prior distributed implementations
Demonstrated scalability up to 256 nodes with competitive single-node performance versus shared-memory libraries

metrics.speedup: 41.7X at 32 nodes vs single node, 6.0X vs state-of-the-art distributed implementation
